discussion_comments.comment_body:
The [request_uri()](https://github.com/pintsized/lua-resty-http/blob/master/lib/resty/http.lua#L792) interface does the `set_keepalive()` automatically for us, so technically this would not be necessary.

However, using the `request_uri()` interface also renders the `conf.keepalive` parameter useless. We should probably use the lower-level `request()` interface instead. This also mean we will need to handle the SSL handshake ourselves, something that the `request_uri()` interface was doing for us.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
the value of `headers["name"]` can be a string or a table, depending on whether the same header was passed more than once in the request, see: https://github.com/openresty/lua-nginx-module?tab=readme-ov-file#ngxreqget_headers

We should handle the scenario where multiple headers are passed, for example by ignoring the header if passed more than once, or grabbing the first value.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Seems there's a mismatch limitation between openresty and nginx that I've ignored, that is,

- nginx allows multiple line values for headers like "Content-Type".

- And openresty defines a list of headers that is "built-in single value", which includes `"Content-Type"`. `ngx.req.set_header` will not allow multiple value for `"Content-Type"`, so if we  `ngx.req.set_header("Content-Type", {"json1", "json2"})` , it will use the last elem as the single value, so then `ngx.req.get_headers()["Content-Type"]` and `ngx.var.http_content_type` will all get a single value `"json2"` .

- But when multiple content type header is sent by http request client, not by openresty set_header API, then the header value is just handled by nginx, and `get_headers` will get a table `{"json1", "json2"}` and `ngx.var.http_content_type`  will get the value as comma separated string: `"json1, json2"`.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Unfortunately this way of parsing query parameters leaves out edge cases. In particular, it is "valid"⁺ to use the same name for a parameter multiple times:

```
http://foo.bar?id=1&id=2&id=3
```

With the current approach, the resulting url would lose the first two values:

```
http://foo.bar?id=3
```

This also makes me think that when two tables are "to be merged", they should include parameters from both. So:

```
http://foo.bar?id=1
```
Merged with
```
http://foo.bar?id=2
```

Should result in
```
http://foo.bar?id=1&id=2
```

[resty.ada.search](https://bungle.github.io/lua-resty-ada/modules/resty.ada.search.html) could be used to parse these parameters instead. Note that [get_all](https://bungle.github.io/lua-resty-ada/modules/resty.ada.search.html#get_all) returns an array instead of a single value.


---
⁺ The http protocol does not actually specify how the query parameters work ([SO thread](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/1746507/authoritative-position-of-duplicate-http-get-query-keys)). It's up to the server. At Kong we try to catch "as wide a net as possible" when we find these cases.

The thinking behind keeping the query params in `location` was that you could set a known safe query value e.g.  in an OAuth flow and know that they wouldn't be overwritten.

I'll remove the merging logic altogether as it's not been requested, and leads to more questions than it solves
